name: Patrick O'Hara
role: Medora coal dealer, partner in the Medora coal company
bio: Patrick 'Pat' O'Hara was a Medora coal man who in November 1884 announced that he would deliver no more coal on Sundays, with orders taken at the Cow Boy office. The paper often printed jokes and quips about him and his growing family. In June 1885, as a member of the Medora coal Co., he bought Mrs. Julia Lason's house in Little Missouri to move to Medora, and he sold it again in July. In January 1886 his coal-mining partnership with A. T. Packard was dissolved, and he went to Helena.

moments.label: Announced no more Sunday coal deliveries

Mr. Patrick O'Hara of the Medora coal Co., has bought Mrs. Julia Lason's house in Little Missouri, and will move it to Medora in a few weeks.
Pat O'Hara has sold his house in Little Missouri, formerly occupied by Mrs. Lason. The present owner intends furnishing and renting it.

Notice is hereby given that on Jan. 16, 1886, the partnership heretofore existing between A. T. Packard and Patrick O'Hara in the coal-mining business, was dissolved by mutual consent. The business will be continued by A. T. Packard and W. F. [Vandriesche?].
Pat. O'Hara has gone to Helena.
